speaker: scene
name: scene
text: Agenda: Welcome

speaker: offsite-moderator
name: Hannah Brooks
text: Good morning everyone! 👋 Thrilled to be here at The Old Mill with you all. I'm Hannah, and I'll be helping us keep this day moving. We've got a jam-packed agenda: icebreaker, Victor's review, a brainstorm with voting, a story game after lunch, and finishing with commitments. Let's get started!

speaker: victor-hale
name: Victor Hale
text: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for making the time for this off-site. I appreciate the hard work of every one of you this past year. I hope today helps us all see how we can work even better together moving forward. VH.

speaker: scene
name: scene
text: Agenda: Icebreaker: two truths and a lie

speaker: offsite-moderator
name: Hannah Brooks
text:
Right, let's get the energy up a bit! 🚀 We're moving onto the "Two Truth and a Lie" icebreaker.

Here's the deal: We’ll go around the group, and each person will post three statements about themselves—two that are totally true and one that is a clever fabrication.

The rule is, everyone else has to guess which one is the lie before the person reveals the answer! We'll tally the scores at the end. 😉

Nina, you’re up first! Tell us your three statements.

speaker: nina-kovac
name: Nina Kovač
text:
1. I moved to England at 22 knowing nobody here.
2. I once tracked 4,000 cars in a single month.
3. I speak three languages — Croatian, German and a bit of Italian.

speaker: maria-santos
name: Maria Santos
text:
GUESS: 2 I don't believe anyone could track 4,000 cars in a month, Nina — even you! 😄

1. I once handled a VIP check-in for a footballer who arrived with a parrot on his shoulder.
2. I left Porto at 20 with two suitcases and no English beyond "hello" and "thank you".
3. I ran a team of five on rotating shifts at a hotel before coming here.

speaker: sofia-marin
name: Sofia Marin
text:
GUESS: 2, The parrot story sounds like a real customer interaction!
1. I trained as an Automotive Engineer in Cluj-Napoca.
2. I spend my free time studying the BMS software for various EV models.
3. I once designed a miniature electric vehicle for a university competition that achieved autonomous flight.

speaker: james-okafor
name: James Okafor
text:
GUESS: 3 Nice try Sofia, autonomous flight? 😄 I'd buy the uni EV project, but flying is a step too far!

1. I started out fitting tyres at Kwik Fit before I ever sat behind a service desk.
2. I once sold a service plan to a customer within five minutes of meeting them.
3. I played semi-pro football for Sutton United back in the day.

speaker: lucas-meyer
name: Lucas Meyer
text:
GUESS: 3. Sports require rhythm, which is different from the rhythm of an engine.
1. I have worked on BMW engines for 30 years.
2. I spend my weekends restoring old BMW motorbikes.
3. I once competed in the Porsche Carrera Cup series.

speaker: mark-doyle
name: Mark Doyle
text:
GUESS: 3 I think you're bluffing on the Porsche Cup, Lucas.
1. Back in '96 we had a 7 Series in for a fortnight waiting on one specific bolt.
2. I coach the under-12s in the parish every summer.
3. I taught myself how to bypass the portal using only a rotary phone.

speaker: daniel-reed
name: Daniel Reed
text:
GUESS: 3 Sounds like a wild day in the office!
1. I’ve been working at VXC for long enough to have seen the turnover in this site from five different models.
2. I once won a local football tournament while working in my retail job.
3. I have a secret garage full of classic BMW E30s waiting for me to buy.

speaker: priya-nair
name: Priya Nair
text:
GUESS: 3 I highly doubt you have a secret garage.
1. I managed to reduce our average debtor days from 34 to 19 in my first two years here.
2. I am working towards my ACCA qualification with the goal of becoming VXC's Finance Director.
3. I once spent an entire weekend tracking down a discrepancy involving a single invoice for exactly 1,240.00 GBP.

speaker: aisha-rahman
name: Aisha Rahman
text:
GUESS: 3 The 1,240.00 exact amount feels too oddly specific to be invented, Priya — but a whole weekend? You'd have billed it as overtime! 😄
1. I was the only girl on my apprenticeship intake at Listers.
2. I wrote a Python script that reads our diagnostic logs and flags known fault patterns.
3. I raced go-karts competitively as a teenager and once beat a future BTCC driver.

speaker: tom-becker
name: Tom Becker
text:
GUESS: 3 Hang on, beating a future BTCC driver?! Aisha, if that's true you've been sandbagging us!! 😄
1. I sold the dealership's first-ever M3 Touring.
2. I raced karts as a teenager and still do track days at Thruxton.
3. I once did 20 car handovers in a single week at my old job.

speaker: elena-popescu
name: Elena Popescu
text:
GUESS: 3 No way Tom, 20 handovers in one week? The paperwork alone would finish you. 😄
1. I started as an apprentice at Dacia in Bucharest before BMW ever heard my name.
2. I was one of the first women in my region to qualify as a BMW Master Technician.
3. I once drove a 3 Series flat out on the Nürburgring Nordschleife on a company jolly.

speaker: victor-hale
name: Victor Hale
text:
GUESS: 3, Nürburgring seems a bit too comfortable for a 'jolly'.
1. I started washing cars for my first job in 1994.
2. I successfully turned around a site that failed two BMW audits.
3. I can parallel park a car while cycling.

speaker: nina-kovac
name: Nina Kovač
text: GUESS: 3 Cycling and parallel parking at the same time sounds like a health and safety incident waiting to happen, Victor 😄 sorry!

speaker: scene
name: scene
text: Icebreaker results. The lies: Maria's lie was #1: "I once handled a VIP check-in for a footballer who arrived with a parrot on his shoulder."; Sofia's lie was #3: "I once designed a miniature electric vehicle for a university competition that achieved autonomous flight."; Lucas's lie was #3: "I once competed in the Porsche Carrera Cup series."; Mark's lie was #3: "I taught myself how to bypass the portal using only a rotary phone."; Daniel's lie was #3: "I have a secret garage full of classic BMW E30s waiting for me to buy."; Tom's lie was #3: "I once did 20 car handovers in a single week at my old job."; Elena's lie was #3: "I once drove a 3 Series flat out on the Nürburgring Nordschleife on a company jolly."; Victor's lie was #3: "I can parallel park a car while cycling.". Correct guesses: James, Mark, Daniel, Priya, Elena, Victor, Nina. Got away with it: Maria.

speaker: offsite-moderator
name: Hannah Brooks
text: That was brilliant! 🎉 You all certainly brought the creativity and the drama to the chat today. Maria, you were a master of disguise! Thanks for such a fun start. Let's dive into the agenda now, and I'll hand the floor over to Victor for the business review.

speaker: scene
name: scene
text: Agenda: Business review

speaker: victor-hale
name: Victor Hale
text: We sold 176 units this year. Tom Becker and Sofia Marin, you both delivered excellent results with 82 units each. However, we had 11 units in October, which is below plan. We are losing 77 sales to competitors, which is a reputation issue we need to address. Let’s see how we can improve our lead conversion from web and walk-ins. VH.

speaker: victor-hale
name: Victor Hale
text: 1,395 job cards this year, split 711 Lucas and 684 Aisha, so both bays are carrying the load fairly. Warranty share is 9.6%, which I want higher, because warranty work is paid work and it keeps the customers coming back. Service invoiced 510,315 GBP net against 5,387,499 GBP on vehicles, and that service line is what pays the rent when the car market wobbles. Finance from Priya: only 4 unpaid invoices outstanding, totalling 1,675 GBP, which is tidy, but I'd still like them collected before Christmas. VH.

speaker: victor-hale
name: Victor Hale
text: The outlook is clear. Our reputation is the asset here, and we must protect it. My three priorities are simple: first, significantly boosting our lead conversion rates to halt the loss of sales to competitors; second, future-proofing our service operations for the full electric transition; and third, ensuring every one of those twelve staff members is developing the skills they need to survive the next decade. I want to hear your thoughts on how we achieve that. VH.

speaker: offsite-moderator
name: Hannah Brooks
text:
Thanks for that, Victor — three clear priorities, and a healthy dose of numbers to chew on. 💪

Now it's over to you all. I'd like four of you to ask Victor a question each — one at a time, please, so we keep this tidy. I'll call on people in this order: Aisha first, then Tom, then James, then Priya.

Aisha, kick us off with your question for Victor. 🔧

speaker: aisha-rahman
name: Aisha Rahman
text: To truly future-proof our service operations for the full electric transition, what concrete plans do we have for upskilling the entire team in complex EV architecture and software diagnostics? 💡

speaker: victor-hale
name: Victor Hale
text: I'm currently liaising with the BMW dealership network to secure the official EV training modules for our lead technicians. I want those skills cascaded across the service department, not just the electrical bays. We need to start rolling out the foundational modules by the end of Q1. VH.

speaker: tom-becker
name: Tom Becker
text: Alright Victor, 82 units each but October's 11 — is my gross per unit part of the lead conversion fix, or are we chasing volume and I just need to flog more metal at list? 😄 Because I'll happily take more web leads, but I want to know which number you're actually grading me on!!

speaker: victor-hale
name: Victor Hale
text: It's not just volume, Tom. I grade based on the overall profitability and the standard of the sale. If we are losing sales to competitors, that hurts the reputation and the long-term margin. Focus on securing the lead, and we’ll discuss the numbers. VH.

speaker: james-okafor
name: James Okafor
text: Victor, from a service side, I understand the need for better conversion on the sales front. But how can we ensure the service experience itself is so outstanding that once a customer trusts us, they automatically stick with us for the long haul, regardless of which sales route they use? 🤔

speaker: victor-hale
name: Victor Hale
text: James, the service experience must be flawless, period. Every single interaction must uphold the reputation of VXC. We need our Service Advisors and technicians to deliver not just repairs, but trust. That customer loyalty is the foundation of our business. VH.

speaker: priya-nair
name: Priya Nair
text: Victor, 82 units each from Tom and Sofia plus 11 in October doesn't tie to 176 — that leaves only 1 unit for the rest of us, so which figures am I reconciling against the DMS? And if lead conversion is priority one, can I have the discount policy in writing before any new scheme starts, so commission and margin stay defensible?

speaker: scene
name: scene
text: Victor Hale's message did not come through.

speaker: scene
name: scene
text: Agenda: Brainstorm and vote

speaker: offsite-moderator
name: Hannah Brooks
text:
Looks like Victor's message took a little nap on the way! No stress, let's carry the energy forward. ⚡️

We’re shifting gears into our brainstorm round! The challenge for everyone is this: What is one concrete idea that would make VXC Motors loved by *both* our customers and our staff by next October?

Keep it focused, give it a short, snappy title, and let's get those bold ideas out. I want to hear from every single department here.

We’re going around the room in this order: Daniel, Priya, Sofia, Tom, Lucas, Maria, Nina, Aisha, Mark, Victor, James, Elena.

Daniel, you’re up first!

speaker: daniel-reed
name: Daniel Reed
text:
IDEA: The Momentum Margin Mastery Program
We need a competitive sales challenge that rewards *quality* conversion and positive customer feedback, not just raw unit volume. This gets the team focused on winning the sale right, keeping the margin solid, and building that essential reputation.

speaker: priya-nair
name: Priya Nair
text:
IDEA: Standardised Deal Transparency & Margin Framework
This framework formalises the deal file review process across all sales, ensuring commission calculations are traceable and every discount is backed by a documented rationale. This guarantees fairness for the team and financial clarity for the business.

speaker: sofia-marin
name: Sofia Marin
text:
IDEA: EV Buyer Education & Conversion Initiative
We need a standardized, technical consultation process that focuses on TCO and real-world range data, rather than high-pressure sales. This builds customer trust and ensures we are selling the right car, protecting our reputation and driving conversions through education.

speaker: tom-becker
name: Tom Becker
text:
IDEA: M Track Day Experience Club
Give every customer who buys an M car or approved used performance model a free track day invite at Thruxton — hot laps, a bit of coaching, the works. Customers become evangelists who come back and send their mates, and honestly it sells itself, I'd run it myself!! 🏁

speaker: lucas-meyer
name: Lucas Meyer
text:
IDEA: First-Time Fix Promise
If a car comes back for the same fault within 30 days, we fix it free and the customer gets a written explanation of what went wrong. Measured properly, diagnosed properly, fixed once — that is how a workshop earns the trust Victor is talking about.

speaker: maria-santos
name: Maria Santos
text:
IDEA: Seamless Digital & Physical Customer Journey
We must ensure every customer, from their first CRM entry to their final service booking, receives a standardized, five-star welcome. This foundational consistency builds immediate trust and protects our reputation across every touchpoint, making us the most reliable choice in the market.

speaker: nina-kovac
name: Nina Kovač
text:
IDEA: Zero-Defect Vehicle Readiness Gateway Checklist
It involves a standardized digital pre-service check that guarantees every single recall and technical bulletin is addressed before a completed before a vehicle leaves the workshop. This ensures we build customer trust because they never have to come back for a mistake that we should have already known about.

speaker: aisha-rahman
name: Aisha Rahman
text:
IDEA: Predictive Fault Analysis Dashboard
We should leverage our diagnostic data to proactively flag known failure patterns before they become customer complaints. This moves us from reactive fixing to preventative maintenance, solidifying our reputation as the absolute experts in EV technology.

speaker: mark-doyle
name: Mark Doyle
text:
IDEA: VOR in 60 Minutes Club
Guarantee any genuine part ordered VOR is on a technician's bench within the hour, or the labour wait's on us. Back in '96 we lost a customer over one bolt — the fastest parts desk in the county is why the lads never wait and why the customers keep coming back.

speaker: victor-hale
name: Victor Hale
text:
IDEA: VXC Customer Trust and Standards Framework
It is about making sure every car leaving our lot meets the highest possible standard, regardless of the sales target. This protects our reputation, which is our most valuable asset, and ensures we are building a stable business.

speaker: james-okafor
name: James Okafor
text:
IDEA: Ask-for-James Loyalty Hotline
Every out-of-plan customer gets a personal check-in call from their advisor before their MOT or service is due — not a marketing text, a proper "how's the car, anything bothering you?" chat. Loyalty is built between visits, and it's the cheapest lead we'll ever get.

speaker: elena-popescu
name: Elena Popescu
text:
IDEA: VXC Master Quality & Zero Comback Guarantee
We need a mandatory, signed sign-off checklist at every handover to certify both quality and completed work. This standard protects my team from blame, eliminates preventable comebacks, and ensures we deliver the verifiable reliability the customers expect, which is the true key to repeat business.

speaker: scene
name: scene
text: Idea board: 1. The Momentum Margin Mastery Program (Daniel) | 2. Standardised Deal Transparency & Margin Framework (Priya) | 3. EV Buyer Education & Conversion Initiative (Sofia) | 4. M Track Day Experience Club (Tom) | 5. First-Time Fix Promise (Lucas) | 6. Seamless Digital & Physical Customer Journey (Maria) | 7. Zero-Defect Vehicle Readiness Gateway Checklist (Nina) | 8. Predictive Fault Analysis Dashboard (Aisha) | 9. VOR in 60 Minutes Club (Mark) | 10. VXC Customer Trust and Standards Framework (Victor) | 11. Ask-for-James Loyalty Hotline (James) | 12. VXC Master Quality & Zero Comback Guarantee (Elena)

speaker: offsite-moderator
name: Hannah Brooks
text:
Wow, the ideas are fantastic! It’s clear we all share a massive focus on building trust and elevating the customer experience, whether it's through technical precision or sales strategy. A lot of these brilliant concepts bridge the gap between our operational strength and the customer’s perception of us.

speaker: aisha-rahman

speaker: mark-doyle

text:

These proposals address the necessary structural integrity of the business and the operational standards required to protect our reputation and margins.

I think making customers feel totally safe with the technical quality and giving them the real facts about the cars are the biggest wins for our reputation.

These two ideas are the only ones that establish clear technical standards and process controls to ensure quality and eliminate avoidable comebacks.

What a vote! 🗳️ Here are your top three:

Victor, over to you: in one message, will you back these three, and if so, what does backing them look like in practice?

speaker: victor-hale
name: Victor Hale
text: I fully back those three. A commitment to quality over quantity is what defines us. Lucas, you own the First-Time Fix Promise and define the metrics for success. Sofia, you own the EV Education Initiative; we need to protect our reputation on the tech side. Elena, I expect you to mandate and enforce the Zero-Defect Gateway across every single job in the workshop. VH.

text: Lunch break at The Old Mill. The chat goes quiet for an hour.

speaker: scene
name: scene
text: Agenda: Story game: a customer's perfect day

speaker: offsite-moderator
name: Hannah Brooks
text:
Welcome back, everyone! Hope you all enjoyed the food and the break. ☀️ 

Let's dive back into the fun with our final activity: 'A customer's perfect day at VXC Motors in 2027'. The challenge is simple: each of you will add exactly ONE sentence to the story, ensuring it flows and ideally reflects how your role makes the day excellent for the customer.

I’ll kick us off. The story begins: A customer named Sam calls, wakes up, and remembers their BMW's service is today.

The order is: James, Aisha, Victor, Daniel, Elena, Priya, Tom, Nina, Mark, Sofia, Maria, and Lucas.

James, you're up first!

speaker: james-okafor
name: James Okafor
text: I greeted Sam with a big smile on the other end of the line and assured them there was no problem at all; we were going to make their day seamless.

speaker: aisha-rahman
name: Aisha Rahman
text: Sam rolls in at 9 sharp, and I've already isolated and tagged the high-voltage system before they've finished their coffee — because the only surprise at VXC should be how quick we are. ⚡😊

speaker: victor-hale
name: Victor Hale
text: The standards I set in this building mean Sam knows every part of their day will be executed perfectly, because our promise is everything.

speaker: daniel-reed
name: Daniel Reed
text: My team and I make sure every single step of their day is a winning play, ensuring the service is absolutely top-tier and the relationship with VXC is set for a massive future victory.

speaker: elena-popescu
name: Elena Popescu
text: I rigorously reviewed the service checklist and assigned the specific priorities to the team to guarantee a zero-combacks solution.

speaker: priya-nair
name: Priya Nair
text: I made sure the entire job file was impeccably documented and the associated financial metrics were traceable, ensuring the entire process was as auditable as it was efficient.

speaker: tom-becker
name: Tom Becker
text: Then, I come over to congratulate them and immediately start discussing the M3 Touring's potential lap times, getting them hyped for their next track day! 🏎️💨

speaker: nina-kovac
name: Nina Kovač
text: I meticulously ran the vehicle through our readiness gateway, confirming that every single technical bulletin and recall was addressed before the car even stepped out of the bay.

speaker: mark-doyle
name: Mark Doyle
text: I'd already got the VOR brake pads on Lucas's bench before Sam's coffee went cold, so the car was ready by lunchtime — 34 years of knowing which bin to reach into, that's the trick 😄

speaker: sofia-marin
name: Sofia Marin
text: While Sam waits, I grab ten minutes to walk them through their charging history and real-world range numbers on the iX, so they drive home knowing exactly what their car can do — no guesswork, no sales pitch, just the facts. ⚡

speaker: maria-santos
name: Maria Santos
text: The moment Sam walks back through the door, I’m there with a fresh coffee and a clear update on the service, ensuring they feel truly valued from the start.

speaker: lucas-meyer
name: Lucas Meyer
text: I ran the final ISTA checks, verified the repair, and confirmed the engine is operating within optimal parameters.

speaker: offsite-moderator
name: Hannah Brooks
text: Sam drives away at 4pm with a spotless car, a full charge, and a smile, already looking forward to the next visit — and that one sentence shows the whole day only worked because every single one of you handed something perfect to the next person, from reception to parts to the workshop floor. Brilliant finish, everyone! 🎉

speaker: scene
name: scene
text: Agenda: Commitments and shout-outs

speaker: offsite-moderator
name: Hannah Brooks
text:
Fantastic work, everyone! Seeing Sam's perfect day unfold was brilliant and a perfect summary of what we aim to achieve together. ✨

For our final moment, let's lock in what we're taking back to the office. Please share one concrete, actionable commitment for the next quarter that ties into one of our successful ideas, and one thank-you shout-out to a colleague from a different department. Keep it concise!

speaker: james-okafor
name: James Okafor
text: COMMIT: Next quarter, I'm committing to formalizing a dedicated post-service check-in call process for every customer—not just the big jobs—to make sure we’re building those real relationships. THANKS: Aisha for being such a sharp technician; the way you explain the tech to people makes it so much easier for me to sell the trust! 😅

speaker: nina-kovac
name: Nina Kovač
text:
COMMIT: I want to commit to refining our Zero-Defect Gateway Checklist by creating a standardized digital review log, so we can track every single recall and bulletin check with absolute certainty and reduce manual cross-checking errors.
THANKS: Mark for being so reliably fast with parts availability; knowing VOR is ready makes my process much less stressful.

speaker: tom-becker
name: Tom Becker
text:
COMMIT: I'm committing to smashing my Q4 sales targets and leading the board in units sold to prove that high-performance cars demand high-performance sales!
THANKS: Maria for always making sure the customer experience is top-tier right from the moment they step onto the showroom floor! 🏁🎉

speaker: mark-doyle
name: Mark Doyle
text:
COMMIT: I'll get the VOR in 60 Minutes Club off the ground — chasing the van drivers and my BMW contacts so workshop VOR parts are on the bench inside the hour, measured every week. The First-Time Fix only works if the parts are there when Lucas needs them.
THANKS: Lucas, for the 20 years of telling me exactly what's wrong before I've even found the part number 😄 makes my job a doddle.

speaker: maria-santos
name: Maria Santos
text:
COMMIT: I'm going to formalize a proactive customer communication process in the CRM, ensuring all customers get a status update at least every 24 hours during service, so they never have to worry about us behind the scenes.
THANKS: Mark for his constant efficiency with parts and supplies; knowing the VOR is available makes my job of keeping promises so much easier! 🧡

speaker: daniel-reed
name: Daniel Reed
text:
COMMIT: I'm committing to reviewing every single deal against our margin KPIs this next quarter, ensuring we're closing deals with the right balance of speed and profitability, because standing still is going backward.
THANKS: Lucas for his commitment to the First-Time Fix Promise; it’s the kind of high-quality foundation that makes selling a winning game. 🏆

speaker: aisha-rahman
name: Aisha Rahman
text:
COMMIT: I’m going to formalize my diagnostic log parsing script into a visual dashboard for the EV bay to track common fault patterns, allowing us to proactively solve issues before they even become official repair points.
THANKS: Nina for championing the Zero-Defect Gateway; it’s the perfect framework for making sure we always nail the root cause. 💡

speaker: victor-hale
name: Victor Hale
text:
COMMIT: I'm committing to a quarterly reputation audit, reviewing every customer complaint and positive review to ensure our promise is met 10,000 times as promised.
THANKS: Maria for keeping the CRM running smoothly; you keep the record clean so I can keep the business steady. VH.

speaker: sofia-marin
name: Sofia Marin
text:
COMMIT: I commit to creating a standardized Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) calculator for our fleet buyers, specifically modeling real-world charging curves and tax benefits for the i5 and iX to ensure our sales advice is entirely data-driven.
THANKS: Mark for his VOR parts delivery process; having the right components ready drastically simplifies my handover conversations and lets me focus purely on the vehicle's technical capabilities. 🔋

speaker: priya-nair
name: Priya Nair
text:
COMMIT: I am committing to standardizing the sales deal review checklist to ensure every discount is fully documented and aligned with our policy before it hits the final invoicing stages.
THANKS: Daniel for focusing on the margin KPIs; knowing those figures are solid makes my month-end close considerably less stressful.

speaker: elena-popescu
name: Elena Popescu
text:
COMMIT: I will run the First-Time Fix Promise with Lucas — a comeback review on every failed job within 48 hours, root cause logged, and the findings fed straight into Nina's Zero-Defect Gateway checklist so the same fault never comes back through my doors.
THANKS: Mark, for 34 years of knowing which bin to reach into before I've even finished the sentence — the VOR promise only works because you make it work. 🧡

speaker: lucas-meyer
name: Lucas Meyer
text:
COMMIT: Every job card gets fault, cause, correction — measured, not guessed. And I will put one teaching diagram a week on the workshop wall so the why is passed on, not just the what.
THANKS: Mark for 20 years of trusting my diagnosis before the part number is even confirmed — and for never once asking me if I'm sure.

name: Victor Hale
